title: Recent-first memory bootstrap for new users
outcome: A newly onboarded user gets useful memories from their last 14 days within 10 minutes, at under $0.05 per user; older history is processed in the background.

criteria.behavior: A new user's first agent turn after bootstrap can read at least one memory saved from their last 14 days.
A rejected database commit never leaves a published memory file that looks committed.
An older task never resurrects a fact the user explicitly forgot.
p95 time from signup to first useful memory is under 10 minutes for the first 50 pilot users.
Saved memories match the gold set's expected facts (quality, not a release gate).

decisions.question: Process full history up front, or recent-first with background backfill?
decisions.chosen: recent-first (14 days), backfill later at low priority
decisions.why: First useful memory in minutes instead of hours; 80% less work before the user sees value.

challenge.simplest: Reuse the existing per-message writer on the last 14 days only; no new service.
challenge.existingMayBeWrong: The current writer assumes one source at a time; bootstrap reads many sources at once and may exhaust the model rate limit.
challenge.scale: 1,200 new users/week at p95 900 sources each: 1.1M source reads/week, about 40 model calls/user, 8 concurrent bootstraps.
failureModes: Rate limits stretch bootstrap past the latency target
Backfill rewrites a fact the user forgot during bootstrap
Publication races the database commit and leaves a half-written file
challenge.e2eProof: Integration test on real Postgres that bootstraps a seeded user, then a failure-injection test that kills the commit after publish.

alternatives.name: full history first
alternatives.why: Simple, but hours before the first memory and 5x the cost for users who churn in week one

alternatives.name: recent-first + background backfill
alternatives.why: Value in minutes; the backfill can be throttled or dropped

alternatives.name: existing saved memory + recent only, no backfill
alternatives.why: Cheapest; loses older context some users rely on

assumptions.text: 14 days of history holds enough to produce a useful memory for most users
assumptions.evidence: Sampled 40 pilot users: 36 had a usable fact within 14 days (notebook link in design.md)

assumptions.text: The customer cohort is about 1,200 new users/week

users.basis: new users per week from the sales forecast; unverified (see assumptions)

workPerUser.ref: query in design.md over 31 pilot users

firstResult.basis: 40 calls x 6 s at concurrency 8, from the measured call time

fullCompletion.basis: p95 sources x measured per-source time, throttled to 2 workers

perUser.basis: 40 calls x 2.5k tokens at the current model price

capacity.cut80: Yes: recent-first skips about 85% of sources before the first memory; the backfill is optional and throttled.

integration.deployPlan: Deploy the reader (MEM-11) first, then this writer behind the bootstrap switch; enable for 5 pilot users, then 50.
